summary: Phase 1C Turn B — Contract Value Resolver. Ran the main-agent-authored /app/backend/tests/test_phase1c_turn_b.py (31 tests: pure unit + live-backend integration) — all 31 pass on first run against the live preview backend. Added /app/backend/tests/test_phase1c_turn_b_complement.py (10 additional tests) to close gaps in the review-request checklist: (a) MONTHLY_FEE Decimal quantisation (99.999 → £100.00, no float drift; £1,000.00 exact; null → error), (b) provenance triple (source + resolver + format_applied) present on every resolved value both in the pure resolver output AND on the frozen contract_variables body, (c) refresh_history[0] full field-set (reason + previous_resolved_at + previous_resolved_by + previous_values_sha256 + refreshed_at + refreshed_by), (d) contract_audit collection entry for 'contract.variables.refresh' verified directly via Mongo (no public /audit HTTP surface exists yet — see review comment) with matching reason, actor, previous_values_sha256, values_sha256, (e) refresh-before-freeze → 400 with '/resolve-variables' in the message, (f) /preview endpoint reflects HQ overrides on both AGREEMENT_DATE ('15 January 2027') and CONTRACT_REFERENCE (upper-cased 'CM-LEGACY-9999') with source pointing at contracts.* and NO persistence (contract_variables stays null post-preview), (g) Phase 1B / Turn A regression: marker library still exactly 29 seed entries, TERRITORY_MAP_URL entry shape (data_type=hyperlink, formula=frozen_territory_map_link, format.requires_frozen_snapshot=true, eligible_contract_types includes territory_amendment), Paloma template c12c8ce1-…-fa23 still status='draft', /api/admin/markers-library returns 29 items. Combined Turn A + Turn B run: 69 passed / 1 documented skip / 0 failed in 27s.
critical_code_review_comments: contract_audit collection has NO public HTTP read surface — a /admin/contracts/{id}/audit (or /admin/contract-audit?contract_id=X) endpoint is missing. Ops / support have to shell into Mongo to trace who refreshed a contract and why. Recommend adding a read-only admin endpoint that returns the audit trail (freeze + refresh events with actor/at/reason/values_sha256) so the immutability + refresh-with-reason contract can be verified from the UI. The complement test worked around this by querying Mongo directly.

contracts_routes.refresh_variables (~L482–550) blocks refresh when contract.status != 'draft', but the error message says 'variables can only be refreshed on drafts' — with Turn C imminent (issued PDFs), HQ will almost certainly need to refresh variables ONLY on drafts, then re-issue. Worth documenting this decision inline as a comment so it doesn't get relaxed accidentally.

resolver.freeze_report_into_contract writes refresh_history + values_sha256 + resolved_at/by inside contract_variables — sha256 is computed over the serialised values map. If value-map field ordering ever becomes non-deterministic (dict insertion order changes across resolver refactors), the hash would drift silently. Add a unit test that freezes the SAME inputs twice and asserts identical sha256 to lock the serialisation-order contract.

contract_variables.refresh_history is an unbounded array on the contract doc — a contract that goes through 500 refreshes will grow the doc past Mongo's 16MB limit. Consider capping the inline history to N=50 and spilling older entries to the contract_audit collection (which already has them).

TERRITORY_MAP_URL library entry stores requires_frozen_snapshot inside .format (not top-level). Not wrong, but the flag governs a HARD-FAIL at resolve time — arguably belongs at top level next to eligible_contract_types + value_source so it's obvious to a reviewer that the marker is gated on frozen state, not just formatted specially.
